United Kingdom Gets Volkswagen's First-Ever Full Hybrid Version of the Popular T-Roc Subcompact CUV
6 photos
Photo: Volkswagen AG
Better late than never applies to Volkswagen and its successful T-Roc subcompact crossover SUV: not long ago we wrote that the all-new, second-generation model is finally coming to Australia in early 2027 , almost two years after it was introduced to the world in the summer of 2025.
Now Volkswagen is finally joining the full hybrid game (!) in the United Kingdom with their first-ever full-hybrid model for the local market: the 2027 VW T-Roc Hybrid can be ordered from November 12 in the country. It also took them long enough: we signaled that the German automaker was finally moving into the regular hybrid powertrain space back in July 2026 when it announced the new powertrain on both the Golf and T-Roc.
Well, at least the United Kingdom is getting one of them – the Volkswagen T-Roc Hybrid will be available in three versions (Match, Style, and R-Line) with on-the-road recommended retail prices starting from £33,725 including VAT. That’s around $45k at the current exchange rate, which isn’t cheap by any standards – especially when the Chinese compete with the already established Western and Asian players for a piece of the pie and come with subversive pricing.
Anyway, Volkswagen offers the T-Roc Hybrid , which combines the ubiquitous 1.5 TSI engine with an electric battery and motor, sitting between the gasoline and PHEV models. “The T-Roc Hybrid is especially suitable for commuters in urban areas, where it combines enhanced fuel economy with low CO2 emissions and the smooth, comfortable driving experience of an electric vehicle,” says the brand, and it’s also compliant with the current ultra-low emission zone (ULEZ) requirements across the UK.
Customers will have a choice of three grades and two different powertrain versions: “the equipment-rich Match, sporty Style and the smart, polished R-Line.” Additionally, all feature the base HEV option of 136 combined ps (134 hp), while Style and R-Line also get a higher output of 170 ps (168 hp). The top version costs £40,500 ($54k), by the way.
All versions have a limited top speed of 112 mph (180 kph) and sprint to 62 mph or 100 kph in 9.7s for the base option or in 8.5s for the high-output variant. Standard features include 18-inch alloy wheels, rear privacy glass, automatic headlights, an eight-inch digital cockpit and 12.9-inch infotainment screen, AC, adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist monitoring, and illuminated Volkswagen logos (Style and R-Line), among other things.
The second-generation Volkswagen T-Roc debuted in the UK earlier this year and has already collected various accolades, including Small SUV of the Year at the 2026 What Car? Awards, among other things. So, what do you think? Does the new Volkswagen T-Roc Hybrid stand a chance against the fierce competition across the United Kingdom or not?
